paper.title: A Comparative Analysis of Techniques and Algorithms for Recognising Sign Language

description: A broad narrative comparison of sign-language recognition techniques, spanning wearable sensors, RGB/depth input and deep-learning architectures.
reason: Meets M1–M3 as a broader review. Table I compares Cui’s iterative-training CSLR method with Papastratis’s context-aware CSLR method, including architectures and datasets, despite also covering many isolated-sign studies.

M1.reason: Paper presents a survey and comparative techniques table.

M2.reason: TableI includes two distinct CSLR studies compared by technique and dataset, identified in refs12–13.

M3.reason: Cui and Papastratis rows describe vision-based methods using PHOENIX video data.

evidence.passage: TableI lists Cui2019 with CNN/temporal convolution/pooling and RWTH-PHOENIX2014, and Papastratis2021 with 2D-CNN/ImageNet and PHOENIX/CSL/GSL. References identify both as continuous sign-language recognition papers.

qualifying_studies: Cui, Liu and Zhang (2019), A Deep Neural Framework for Continuous Sign Language Recognition by Iterative Training [12]
Papastratis, Dimitropoulos and Daras (2021), Continuous Sign Language Recognition through a Context-Aware Generative Adversarial Network [13]

assessments.reason: Retain for full-text assessment because review purpose and possible vision-based CSLR coverage are supported.
